::: {.why}
Every impact model treats order flow as one thing, and the models this week say it is two things with very different consequences, so knowing how well they can be separated matters.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Construct a flow-toxicity measure from your data and say what it is estimating.
- State why the standard measure is contested, and check its behaviour on a day with a known event.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Build a volume-bucketed order imbalance measure: bucket trades by volume rather than by clock time, compute the imbalance in each bucket, and track its rolling distribution. Then check that it rises before large price moves in your sample, which is the property it is supposed to have.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Be careful about the claim: the measure depends on a trade-signing rule and on the bucketing, and published critiques argue that much of its apparent predictive power comes from those choices. Test one of those criticisms yourself by changing the bucket size and reporting how much the result moves.
:::
:::
